readerContract.humanQuestion: How do I turn what I understand about AI into reliable work I can actually use, without handing over judgment, authority or information I am not allowed to share?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: The reader can run one complete responsible AI working loop and keep a small reusable kit: a personal setup, three saved briefs or workflows, a verification habit and a decision rule for when to accept, check, restart or decline AI.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: AI Fundamentals 101 or equivalent familiarity with models, context, tools, retrieval, memory, agents and verification. No coding or technical job experience is assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: Useful AI work is a controlled loop: choose a suitable task, provide allowed and relevant context, define the job and acceptance conditions, inspect what the system produced and actually used, verify in proportion to risk, revise or restart, delegate only within explicit authority, then save the reusable result and its upkeep trigger.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: The same loop applies to an email, document comparison, meeting summary, research question, household plan or read-only recurring briefing; the stakes and required evidence change, but the reader's control points remain visible.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A scannable, resumable practical textbook that integrates the complete working loop. It routes deep briefing, setup, account-safety and verification procedures to their canonical books and routes current vendor behaviour to dated tool cards.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I know what to do next, what not to hand over and how to tell whether the result earned my trust.

strengthsToUse: Begin with recognisable human stakes before naming the mechanism.
Keep the reader's judgment central and the voice warm, exact and useful.
Use humour only when it sharpens a distinction or consequence.
patternsNotToCopy: Do not copy the episode's scene structure or three-tool comparison.
Do not import dated facts or references without current primary evidence.
Do not turn the textbook into an episode transcript.

strengthsToUse: Answer the reader's practical question early.
Separate stable, conditional, current and unknown claims.
Turn evidence boundaries into a precise next action.
patternsNotToCopy: Do not inherit any held or dated claim.
Do not repeat an identical answer scaffold in every chapter.
Do not substitute isolated answers for the complete working loop.

glossaryAccumulation.preventionEvidence: draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure names a cumulative loop and artifact kit.

templateRepetition.producerGuard: Chapters use the form their job needs: comparison, diagnosis, bounded procedure, decision boundary or handoff.

decorativeAnalogy.producerGuard: No analogy is pre-authorised; any retained analogy must clarify a named mechanism and state its limit.

referenceConfetti.preventionEvidence: Humour is optional and the planned practical artifacts carry the teaching.

missingMechanism.producerGuard: Every practical rule explains which part of the task/context/evidence/authority loop changes and why.
missingMechanism.preventionEvidence: draftArchitecture.causalSequence binds seven connected control points.

genericAction.producerGuard: Actions produce a saved brief, test result, evidence trail, authority boundary or handoff—not 'be careful' advice.
genericAction.preventionEvidence: draftArchitecture.usefulAction names the Working With AI Kit.

jargonBeforeMeaning.producerGuard: Start with the visible work problem; introduce terminology only when it improves the next decision.
jargonBeforeMeaning.preventionEvidence: The opening and every chapter begin from a concrete adult task.

disconnectedSystem.producerGuard: Every chapter adds one stage to the responsible working loop and reconnects to the saved artifact kit.

mechanismBeforeMotivation.preventionEvidence: communicationDesign.explanationArc starts with the Tuesday-afternoon inconsistency.

workedExampleOvertakesBookPurpose.preventionEvidence: draftArchitecture.workedCase and transferCase are distinct and bounded.

technicalExplainerVoice.producerGuard: Write as a smart colleague helping the reader get a real result, not as a systems manual proving coverage.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Good AI work is not one magic prompt. It is a controlled loop in which you choose the job, provide allowed and useful context, define the result, inspect the evidence, revise deliberately, constrain any delegated action and keep what is worth reusing.
causalSequence: Choose a task whose risk and review burden make AI assistance worthwhile.
Decide what information is allowed and useful, then place stable and one-job context deliberately.
Define the outcome, audience, source material, constraints and acceptance conditions.
Produce a first result and inspect what the system actually used, omitted or invented.
Verify claims, calculations and decisions in proportion to the cost of error.
Revise once with a precise correction; restart or stop when the method is failing.
For delegated work, bound tools, actions, approvals, stopping conditions and escalation.
Save the accepted artifact, brief, evidence and upkeep trigger so the improvement survives the chat.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A reader turns disorganised meeting notes into a client-ready follow-up: she removes material the tool may not receive, supplies the approved notes, defines audience and acceptance, checks each action against the source, corrects one omission and saves the brief plus final version.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: Without a supplied solution, the reader decides whether and how to use AI for a read-only weekly household or work briefing. She names the source, permissions, allowed action, evidence checks, pause trigger and condition that would make the workflow not worth keeping.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Build a Working With AI Kit containing: one baseline profile, three task briefs or workflows, an allowed-information check, a source-and-claim verification card, a restart rule and a delegation authority line.

humourPlan.lessonJob: Use light workplace and Rewind Era wit only to make inconsistency, generic prose or runaway delegation memorable; the joke must preserve the decision rule.

draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Introduction: promise, prerequisite, boundary and kit. Chapters 1–3 diagnose inconsistency and place context. Chapters 4–6 brief, control and revise. Chapters 7–9 choose task/tool fit and inspect sources/tools. Chapters 10–12 constrain delegation and evaluate against acceptance. Chapter 13 assembles the reusable system. Every chapter adds one named kit artifact, a compact practical action and a causal What’s Next bridge.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Retain predictable retrieval landmarks—objectives, key terms, practical action, What’s Next and quick reference—but vary the teaching form. Do not manufacture a repeated Use/Best for/Watch for/Try this card set, a product tour or a workbook page after every section.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: Use a scannable textbook: practical questions lead, invisible context and evidence paths become concrete, and each chapter lands in a reusable artifact. Do not mimic a presenter, lecture, television segment or Hannah Fry's voice.

humanQuestion.reason: The reader already has a real result that worked once and failed later.
humanQuestion.plannedEvidence: Open with the same Tuesday task producing two different results and the practical cost of not knowing what changed.

usefulCuriosity.reason: Comparing two apparently identical attempts exposes hidden system variables.
usefulCuriosity.plannedEvidence: Ask the reader to predict which changed input, context, tool or evaluation condition explains the difference before revealing the loop.

invisibleProcessConcrete.reason: Context assembly, retrieval, tool use and authority boundaries are mostly invisible in a chat window.
invisibleProcessConcrete.plannedEvidence: Trace one meeting-follow-up task through supplied material, system context, output, evidence check and accepted handoff.

familiarTechnicalMovement.reason: The reader needs enough system language to troubleshoot without turning the book into Fundamentals again.
familiarTechnicalMovement.plannedEvidence: Move from the familiar task to the exact context/tool/evidence distinction, then return to the next practical repair.

limitationsConsequences.reason: Bad context, unsupported output or excessive authority can create privacy, accuracy and workplace consequences.
limitationsConsequences.plannedEvidence: Every affected chapter names what AI cannot establish, what the reader must check and when the task should stop.

humourSurprise.reason: A small earned joke can make a circuit breaker or generic-output symptom easier to remember.
humourSurprise.plannedEvidence: Retain only jokes that encode the rule; cut decorative pop culture and overexplained punchlines.

betterNextQuestion.reason: The book succeeds when the reader can diagnose the next task without memorising a vendor interface.
betterNextQuestion.plannedEvidence: End with: What changed, what evidence did I inspect, what authority did I grant and what is worth saving?

explanationArc.sharedStartingPoint: The same ordinary task works on Monday and disappoints on Tuesday even though the reader thinks she asked the same thing.
explanationArc.curiosityGap: If the prompt looks the same, what actually changed—and which part can the reader control?
mechanismSequence: The surrounding product assembles context, instructions, files, memory or retrieved material that may differ between attempts.
The model generates within that assembled system and any permitted tools, so the visible request is only one input.
The reader defines the job and evidence boundary, then inspects the result against sources and acceptance conditions.
A precise revision, restart or stop decision prevents a bad interaction from becoming a bad workflow.
The accepted brief, evidence and authority boundary are saved outside the fragile conversation.
explanationArc.earnedClick: The inconsistency is not proof that AI is random or that the reader failed to discover a magic prompt; it is a system with several controllable inputs and review points.
explanationArc.smallLanding: Keep the useful bits. Retire the séance.
explanationArc.safetyBoundary: Permission, privacy, source authority and high-stakes checking are answered directly before any playful framing.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: The draft's confident claims about hidden context and invented product memory behaviour can destroy trust even if the rest of the prose is polished.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Rewrite the introduction plus Chapters 2 and 3 as the smallest continuous sample: platform-neutral mechanism, dated official tool-card boundary, one practical context test, one saved profile artifact and explicit privacy/authority limits.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: An unfamiliar reader can explain the difference among visible history, current context, instructions, project material and optional memory; run a clean-thread comparison; and state what she must check in her exact product without repeating a fictive feature or universal limit.
